messages:
kai: Brain-dump: proposal for call-path-aware prefetching in the loader. Idea: use runtime prompt/route hints + recent trace telemetry to prioritize loading only the model blocks/heads likely to be touched. Could cut warmup cost for large decoder models on common paths.
alyssa: Interesting. So instead of treating a shard as monolithic we bias prefetch to a predicted access set?
kai: Exactly. Two inputs: 1) static access map (which layers/chunks contain which submodules), 2) dynamic policy derived from recent RT telemetry (prompt length distribution, common tokens, route). Combine to produce prioritized chunk manifest.
ram: How do we predict accurately? Models can have conditional control flow, long-range attention, or dynamic plugins.
sasha: We should start conservative: predict prefix-heavy paths (first N tokens -> layers 0..K), or top-k heads for short prompts. Use a lightweight ML model trained on per-route traces, but fall back to full warmup when uncertainty high.
marie: Security/compliance: for private deployments strict customers will expect full-verify+full-warmup. This feature should be opt-in and have a strict_consistency toggle.
ishaan: Verification: progressive verify still applies. If we delay loading some chunks, full verify can still run async. But we need to guarantee correctness if runtime touches a delayed chunk  either block on quick verify or fetch+map synchronously.
kai: Config sketch:
```
prefetch:
  strategy: callpath-aware
  min_warmup_pct: 30  # always warm at least 30% of model (critical layers)
  predictor: route_histogram_v1
  uncertainty_threshold: 0.25
```
ram: min_warmup_pct is smart; avoids pathological misses. What about multi-tenant noise on telemetry? Using global route_histogram might bias wrong models.
sasha: Predictor should be scoped: per-customer, per-route, and a global fallback. Also ttl on predictors to forget stale traffic.
marie: Runtime API implications: expose ModelHandle.prefetch_policy(hint) and ModelHandle.require_block(block_id) to let caller pin critical blocks for a latency-critical call. This keeps low-level control for platform teams.
ishaan: Interaction with KV cache and attention cache: if we prefetch only a subset of weights we must still allow KV cache growth. Also prefetch order should respect dependency graph: earlier layers first.
kai: Agreed. Prefetch planner will use dependency DAG + predictor priorities to generate fetch sequence. Also add a fast-path sync fallback: if runtime requests missing chunk and policy=optimistic, block once to fetch and then continue.
alyssa: Metrics to watch: missed_prefetch_rate, incremental_fetch_latency, predictor_misprediction_ratio, warmup_cost_savings_pct. Also alert when missed_prefetch_rate spikes.
ram: Edgecases: model rollouts & hotpatches. Predictor trained on old model version could mispredict new structure. Need predictor versioning tied to manifest epoch and safe fallback to index-first when mismatch.
kai: Good call. We'll bind predictor -> manifest_epoch; on hotpatch increment predictor version and invalidate old predictors. Also add canary flag to run predictor in shadow mode for new model versions.
sasha: Testing: synthetic traces with multiple routes, measure mean first-token latency across strategies: index-first vs callpath-aware vs header-first. Inject a model layout change and verify predictor invalidation.
icebot: loaderbot: CI job created: prefetch/callpath-aware-probe (8 tests queued).
ishaan: Action items:
- kai: prototype planner + config schema by next Tue
- sasha: implement per-route predictor scaffolding (shadow mode) by Wed
- alyssa: add E2E latency tests and metrics plumbing by Mon
- ram: safety toggle + manifest_epoch binding in loader by Thu
- marie: draft rollout plan (dedicated canary -> opt-in beta -> default off for private)
kai: Also we'll add console panels for missed_prefetch_rate and predictor_misprediction_ratio. Start internal canary only.
alyssa: :thumbsup: I like keeping it opt-in and observable.
marie: Note: document tradeoffs in loader README and include a checklist for customers on when to enable (stable model layout, predictable prompts).
kai: I'll open a PoC branch and link here. Ping if you want to pair on the planner.
loaderbot: branch pushed: feature/callpath-prefetch (WIP).
ram: Nice. If we can get 20-30% warmup cost reduction on typical routes that's huge.
sasha: Agreed. But prioritize safety and clear fallbacks.
kai: Will do. Thanks all.
